children: The S&P Global Philippines Manufacturing PMI edged down to 49.1 in October 2026 from 49.6 in September, marking a second consecutive month of contraction as output and new orders continued to decline.
While output fell at a slower pace, the decline in new orders deepened, with firms citing weak demand and hot weather, which some linked to El Niño.
New export orders also contracted modestly.
Manufacturers further reduced purchasing activity, with the decline reaching an 11-month high, while employment fell for a second straight month.
Supplier delivery times also deteriorated for the 11th straight month.
Pre-production inventories were unchanged, while finished goods stocks rose marginally for the first time in four months.
Despite subdued activity, business confidence rebounded to a near two-year high.
Meanwhile, price pressures eased, with input costs rising at their slowest pace in eight months.

title: Philippines Factory Activity Contracts for 2nd Month
